analysis.title: The great silver puke
key_insights: Silver is testing $50 and trades well below its 200-day moving average. The next meaningful support is the long-term trendline in the $46-48 area.
Silver has been more oversold only once since the Liberation Day sell-off. The report notes oversold conditions can persist.
Silver volatility normally rises when price rises (upside skew). In this sell-off volatility is being bid as price falls, which indicates investors are buying downside protection.
Silver has broken its tight inverse relationship with the dollar this year and is sharply underperforming the inverted DXY, so it is no longer simply trading the dollar.

Silver and KOSPI have traded closely, with Korean equities often following silver with a lag. The report attributes the link to momentum, crowded positioning and FOMO in both the silver and AI trades rather than fundamentals.
The report raises the question of whether the AI trade has considerably more room to unwind to the downside after silver's liquidation.
CTAs are already running substantial silver shorts but have room to add as downside momentum builds. Further weakness could trigger another wave of CTA selling and a self-reinforcing momentum unwind.
risk_factors: Further CTA selling could turn the liquidation into a self-reinforcing momentum unwind.
Silver's close tracking of KOSPI suggests the unwind could extend to AI-related equities.
Oversold conditions can persist longer than expected.
vol_and_positioning: Silver volatility is catching aggressive bids as prices fall, reversing its usual upside-skew behavior, which signals panicky demand for downside protection.
CTAs are running substantial silver shorts with room to add, and systematic selling may not be exhausted.
Silver is massively oversold, more so only once since the Liberation Day sell-off.
